paragraphs: A classifier can predict the right label while giving misleading confidence scores. Calibration asks whether those scores reflect how often predictions are correct. This paper develops AdaFocal, a training loss that adjusts its behavior using evidence about whether the model is too confident or insufficiently confident.

The approach builds on focal loss, whose parameter gamma controls an effect that can reduce overconfidence. Earlier sample-dependent choices relied on heuristics. AdaFocal instead updates gamma for different groups of samples using both its previous value and calibration information from a validation set. It draws on the calibration behavior of focal and inverse-focal losses, allowing the adjustment to respond to the direction of the confidence error.

Across image recognition tasks and one language task, covering multiple network architectures, the authors report improved calibration with similar accuracy. They also report substantially better detection of inputs from outside the training distribution. These findings suggest that adapting the loss to observed confidence errors can improve the usefulness of uncertainty estimates alongside ordinary classification performance.
neurips-2022-adafocal-calibration-aware-.tldr: AdaFocal adjusts focal-loss parameters using validation-set confidence errors, improving calibration and out-of-distribution detection in the reported experiments.

paragraphs: A decision system can inherit biased data while also influencing which new outcomes become observable. This paper studies classification with costly, censored feedback: the learner cannot freely obtain all the information it would like. Its goal is to improve the dataset over time through deliberately chosen exploration.

Exploration means occasionally accepting people whom the current rule would reject. These departures from the rule are adaptive and bounded, so the decision maker controls how much exploration occurs. The algorithm includes parameters for balancing the aim of reducing statistical bias against the risks incurred while gathering additional feedback. This makes data collection itself part of the learning problem.

The authors analytically establish that this strategy can debias data for certain distributions, rather than claiming that exploration always removes bias. They also examine how fairness criteria can operate alongside the algorithm and illustrate its behavior on synthetic and real-world datasets. The contribution connects fairer decision making to the process that creates the available evidence, with an explicit tradeoff between learning opportunities and exploration risk.
neurips-2022-adaptive-data-debiasing-thr.tldr: Bounded, adaptive departures from a classification rule can reduce dataset bias under certain distributions while controlling exploration risk.

paragraphs: Learning from label proportions replaces individual training labels with the proportions observed in groups, called bags. This paper studies linear threshold classifiers when some unknown classifier satisfies every supplied bag. The challenge is to recover a classifier that matches many of those proportions despite lacking individual labels.

The authors develop a semidefinite relaxation and a rounding procedure for bags containing at most three examples. Their algorithm guarantees satisfaction of at least one twelfth of the bags. For bags of size q at least four, their techniques give an approximation guarantee proportional to 1/q under a weaker definition of satisfaction. Simulated-data experiments also demonstrate the applicability of the techniques.

The paper complements these algorithms with computational hardness results. For any constant bag size q, satisfying more than approximately a 1/q fraction is NP-hard even when predictions may combine constantly many linear threshold functions. For size two, the hardness threshold improves to approximately 4/9. Together, the results show how larger bags make approximation harder and distinguish achievable guarantees from computational barriers.
neurips-2022-algorithms-and-hardness-for.tldr: The paper gives approximation algorithms and hardness bounds for learning linear thresholds from grouped label proportions, exposing increasing difficulty with larger bags.

paragraphs: Adversarial robustness concerns whether predictions withstand permitted changes to an input. This paper asks whether strong robustness can be obtained from learning algorithms whose predictors are robust on only a small fraction of the data distribution. It calls these starting algorithms barely robust learners.

The authors present an oracle-efficient boosting algorithm that strengthens such learners. A crucial qualification concerns which changes the starting learner must withstand: its robustness must hold for a larger perturbation set. The initial requirement therefore combines limited coverage of the data distribution with robustness against a broader set of input changes. Robustness on a small fraction alone is not the condition used by the result.

The paper shows that the larger-set requirement is necessary for strongly robust learning and that weaker relaxations do not suffice. Its main finding is a qualitative and quantitative equivalence between strong robust learning and this particular form of barely robust learning. This provides a way to characterize the weaker learning capability needed for boosting, while identifying why simply weakening the robustness requirement further would fail.
neurips-2022-boosting-barely-robust-lear.tldr: Barely robust learners can be boosted to strong robustness under a larger-perturbation-set requirement that the paper shows is necessary.

paragraphs: Sparse neural networks retain only part of their available parameters or connections. This paper focuses on controlling how sparse a trained model becomes. Many existing methods encourage sparsity through an extra penalty in the training objective, but choosing its strength requires trial and error because it does not directly specify the final sparsity.

The authors formulate training as a constrained optimization problem with a desired sparsity target. They use an existing gating mechanism to support sparsification, allowing the prediction objective and the target to guide learning together. The practical distinction is that the user specifies the desired model sparsity directly, rather than repeatedly adjusting a penalty and checking what sparsity it produces.

Experiments span CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, TinyImageNet, and ImageNet with WideResNet and ResNet architectures. In these evaluations, the method reliably reaches predetermined sparsity targets without compromising predictive performance. The findings support constrained training as a practical way to make model sparsity controllable while preserving the predictive quality demonstrated in the tested settings.
neurips-2022-controlled-sparsity-via-con.tldr: A constrained training formulation directly targets neural-network sparsity and reliably meets those targets without sacrificing predictive performance in the reported experiments.

paragraphs: Image inpainting fills damaged or missing regions using clues about what belongs there. Those clues include both visual appearance and relationships between meaningful image regions. Many methods obtain this context from the incomplete image itself. This paper expands the available context by learning regional representations across different images.

The proposed Cross-Image Context Memory, or CICM, contains multiple sets of representations associated with different visual patterns. Learning these representations across images gives the inpainting method access to richer contextual information when recovering a corrupted region. The task remains single-image inpainting, but the learned memory brings information from other images into the reconstruction process.

Experiments on several datasets demonstrate the method's effectiveness and generalization, with reported state-of-the-art performance. The results support the idea that useful restoration context extends beyond relationships within an individual image. The central contribution is a memory of cross-image regional patterns that can help reason about missing content, complementing the information supplied by the intact portions of the image being repaired.
neurips-2022-cross-image-context-for-sin.tldr: CICM improves single-image inpainting by using a memory of regional visual patterns learned across multiple images.

paragraphs: A prediction can be useful or harmful depending on the decision made from it. Decision-focused learning trains predictors for the downstream optimization task that consumes their outputs. A major obstacle is that optimization solutions can change discontinuously, making it difficult to obtain useful gradients for training.

This paper learns a task-informed loss function that replaces the optimization component used during predictive-model training. Constructing that loss requires access to a black-box solver for the decision problem, avoiding the need to handcraft a differentiable approximation for every task. The learned loss can also be convex by construction, providing a deliberately structured objective for optimization.

The authors evaluate the approach on three resource allocation problems. It outperforms learning that ignores task structure in all three domains and also surpasses handcrafted surrogates from prior work. The findings support automatically learning how prediction errors affect downstream decisions. The method retains a connection to the actual decision problem through the solver, while moving task-specific information into a loss that can guide predictor training.
neurips-2022-decision-focused-learning-w.tldr: Automatically learned, task-informed losses replace the optimization component of decision-focused training and outperform compared approaches on three resource allocation problems.

paragraphs: Adversarial training needs substantial data, yet complex image augmentations that help ordinary training have not consistently helped it. This paper interprets that problem through domain generalization: augmentations increase variety, but training must also remain relevant to the distribution encountered at test time.

The proposed DAJAT method combines simple and complex augmentations while assigning them separate batch normalization layers. A Jensen-Shannon divergence loss encourages their learning to proceed together, allowing simple augmentations to guide learning from complex ones. This arrangement addresses the tension between exposing the network to diverse examples and preserving a useful connection to test-like data.

For computational efficiency, the authors add ACAT, a two-step adversarial defense using an increasing perturbation-bound schedule and weight-space smoothing to prevent gradient masking. DAJAT achieves a substantially better balance between robustness and accuracy than the compared RobustBench methods on ResNet-18 and WideResNet-34-10. The reported results show that augmentation design and efficient adversarial training can work together when differences between augmentation distributions are explicitly handled.
neurips-2022-efficient-and-effective-aug.tldr: DAJAT jointly learns from simple and complex augmentations to improve the robustness–accuracy tradeoff of adversarial training in the tested networks.

paragraphs: Lewis signaling games study how two agents develop a communication protocol while cooperating on a task. Earlier reinforcement-learning approaches often produced protocols that generalized poorly or lacked compositional structure. This paper analyzes the learning objective to understand why successful cooperation may still yield these undesirable language properties.

The authors show that the standard objective separates into a co-adaptation loss and an information loss. This decomposition exposes two potential sources of overfitting that can interfere with the emergence of structured communication. It gives a more specific account of the problem than treating the agents' overall task performance as a single measure of learning success.

When the authors control overfitting associated with the co-adaptation component, the resulting languages become more compositional and generalize better. The finding links properties of the learned protocol to how the agents fit their shared training problem. It indicates that controlling a particular source of overfitting can improve communication structure, without asserting that every signaling game will naturally produce a generalizable language.
neurips-2022-emergent-communication-gene.tldr: Decomposing the Lewis-game objective reveals overfitting sources, and controlling co-adaptation overfitting produces more compositional, better-generalizing communication.

paragraphs: In a partially observable decision process, an agent must learn to act without directly seeing the underlying state. Existing theoretical algorithms often rely on strong assumptions about the dynamics or on an oracle that solves a computationally hard planning or estimation problem. Such an oracle leaves an important part of the computation unresolved.

This paper gives an end-to-end algorithm for observable POMDPs without relying on those hard subroutines. Observability has a specific meaning here: sufficiently different distributions over hidden states must produce sufficiently different distributions over observations. This assumption supplies a connection between what differs internally and what the agent can distinguish from its observations.

The algorithm runs in quasipolynomial time. Its exploration strategy uses barycentric spanners to construct policy covers, departing from the customary use of optimism under uncertainty. The contribution is therefore a computationally explicit learning result under the stated observability condition. It replaces an assumed hard oracle with an actual end-to-end procedure, while retaining a qualified runtime guarantee and a clear restriction on the environments considered.
neurips-2022-learning-in-observable-pomd.tldr: The paper gives a quasipolynomial-time, oracle-free learning algorithm for POMDPs satisfying a specified observability assumption.

paragraphs: Finding information online can require several hyperlink steps after a search engine reaches the right neighborhood. This paper studies a navigation policy that reads local content and chooses links that move toward a target. Its central question is whether useful navigation can be learned from randomly sampled trajectories.

The authors show that behavioral cloning of those trajectories is sufficient to learn an effective link-selection policy in their setting. They evaluate the approach on a Wikipedia graph containing 38 million nodes and 387 million edges. The model successfully navigates between nodes five steps apart 96% of the time and between nodes twenty steps apart 92% of the time.

The learned embeddings and navigation policy are also used for fact verification and question answering. Combined with basic TF-IDF search and ranking, they achieve results competitive with state-of-the-art methods. These findings connect hyperlink navigation to downstream information tasks: a policy trained from random walks can help acquire relevant information after an initial search, as well as navigate the graph itself.
neurips-2022-learning-to-navigate-wikipe.tldr: Behavioral cloning of random walks learns effective Wikipedia navigation and supports competitive fact verification and question answering when combined with basic search.

paragraphs: Lossy neural image compression trains models to represent images compactly while allowing reconstruction error. Existing methods approximate quantization noise with a uniform posterior and commonly estimate the training gradient from one sample. This paper investigates how using multiple samples can improve that training process.

The starting point is the importance-weighted autoencoder objective, which gives a tighter bound than the usual evidence lower bound and approaches log likelihood as the sample count grows. The authors analyze how the uniform posterior used in compression affects the bias and variance of different gradient estimators. They also explain a commonly used compression-training trick through its effect on gradient variance.

From this analysis, they develop MS-NIC, an enhanced multi-sample objective tailored to neural image compression. Experiments show improvements to state-of-the-art compression methods. The approach is described as plug-and-play and readily extendable to neural video compression. Its contribution lies in adapting the objective and gradient analysis to the particular noise model used in compression, rather than treating additional samples as an automatically sufficient improvement.
neurips-2022-multi-sample-training-for-n.tldr: MS-NIC uses a compression-specific multi-sample training objective to improve existing neural image compression methods.

paragraphs: Generating symbolic music requires handling long sequences while preserving patterns such as repetition across bars. Full Transformer attention becomes expensive for these sequences, and existing models can struggle with musical structure. Museformer addresses both issues by varying how much detail its attention assigns to different bars.

Fine-grained attention reads every token in selected earlier bars that are especially relevant to musical structure. Similarity statistics guide those selections, with examples including bars one, two, four, and eight positions earlier. For the remaining bars, coarse-grained attention reads summaries. This keeps broader context available while reserving detailed attention for relationships considered particularly useful.

The authors report that Museformer can model sequences more than three times longer than its full-attention counterpart. Objective and subjective evaluations also support its ability to produce long music with high quality and improved structure. The findings suggest that selective detail can serve both musical organization and computational efficiency: the model retains direct access to structurally relevant material without processing every past token at the same level.
neurips-2022-museformer-transformer-with.tldr: Museformer combines detailed attention to structurally relevant bars with summaries of other bars to generate longer, better-structured music efficiently.

paragraphs: Stochastic partial differential equations describe systems that evolve across space and time under random influences. This paper introduces Neural SPDEs, an architecture that learns their solution operators from partially observed data. The formulation uses the mathematical notion of a mild solution to connect continuous dynamics with a learnable model.

The architecture brings together capabilities from continuous-time sequence models and neural operators. It can process sequential information at arbitrary spatial resolutions and represent solutions that depend jointly on an initial condition and a particular realization of driving noise. Operations in the spectral domain allow evaluation through either an ordinary differential equation solver or a fixed-point calculation.

Experiments on semilinear stochastic equations, including stochastic Navier-Stokes, demonstrate learning across resolutions. The reported comparisons show better accuracy and lower training-data requirements than alternative models, with speedups reaching three orders of magnitude over traditional solvers. These results support learning continuous spatiotemporal behavior in a form that accommodates changing spatial resolution and explicit random forcing, rather than binding the representation to one fixed sampling grid.
neurips-2022-neural-stochastic-pdes-reso.tldr: Neural SPDEs learn randomly driven spatiotemporal dynamics across spatial resolutions, with improved accuracy, data efficiency, and solver speed in the reported experiments.

paragraphs: Evaluating occupational gender stereotypes requires data that represents gender within occupations in a balanced way. OCCGEN is a toolkit for extracting multilingual parallel datasets with that aim. Its design includes gender diversity beyond a binary distinction, enabling the selection of data intended to represent society more fairly.

The paper presents two uses of the toolkit to build machine-translation evaluation datasets. These cover four high-resource languages from different linguistic families and one low-resource African language. Balancing gender within occupations makes the selected data useful for examining translation behavior across gender subsets and for further work explicitly aimed at mitigating occupational stereotypes.

In the high-resource-language analyses, translation outputs tend to be worse for feminine subsets than for masculine ones. The authors offer an explanation involving reduced attention to the source sentence and greater attention to the already generated target prefix, which favors frequent masculine forms. The contribution combines a data-selection tool with evidence about a translation disparity and a proposed account of how that disparity arises.
neurips-2022-occgen-selection-of-real-wo.tldr: OCCGEN extracts multilingual data balanced by gender within occupations, and its translation evaluations reveal poorer outcomes for feminine subsets in high-resource languages.

paragraphs: Additional unlabeled data can help learning across domains only if the method uses it effectively. Okapi addresses this through online statistical matching. It finds neighboring examples across domains, removes statistical outliers, and uses the resulting pairs as different views whose learned features should agree.

The consistency objective operates on features rather than predicted outputs. This makes the method applicable across different input types and prediction tasks. A memory bank and a slowly updated momentum encoder support matching without excessive runtime or memory demands. Together, these components make cross-domain correspondence an ongoing part of training.

On WILDS 2.0 datasets, Okapi improves out-of-distribution generalization over the compared baselines for iWildCam image classification, PovertyMap image regression, and CivilComments text classification. The results also show that additional unlabeled data can improve on empirical risk minimization with this method. Qualitative inspection finds that learned matches are strongly related in meaning, supporting the idea that statistical matching can create useful consistency relationships across domains.
neurips-2022-okapi-generalising-better-b.tldr: Okapi matches examples across domains and aligns their features, improving out-of-distribution generalization using unlabeled data in the reported evaluations.

paragraphs: Predictive coding is a neuroscience-inspired approach to neural-network training that traditionally performs inference in hierarchical Gaussian generative models. Those distributional assumptions make it difficult to reproduce the behavior of complex layers and activation functions. This paper broadens predictive coding to accommodate arbitrary probability distributions.

That generalization allows internal distributions to fit the architecture and task more flexibly. In particular, it enables training Transformer architectures that are difficult to approximate using only Gaussian assumptions. The authors first investigate differences between the generalized method and standard predictive coding on several toy examples, then evaluate it on larger model families.

For variational autoencoders, the method reaches the same reconstruction quality as backpropagation in the reported experiments. For conditional language modeling, it trains Transformers to performance comparable with backpropagation. These findings support a wider practical scope for predictive coding: loosening its distributional assumptions makes the approach compatible with architectures and tasks beyond those readily captured by its conventional Gaussian formulation.
neurips-2022-predictive-coding-beyond-ga.tldr: Generalizing predictive coding beyond Gaussian distributions enables Transformer training and matches or approaches backpropagation performance in the reported tasks.

paragraphs: Unsupervised mixture learning tries to uncover hidden components from observations that combine them. This paper examines post-nonlinear mixtures, where a linear mixture is subsequently transformed by unknown nonlinear functions applied separately to its elements. Removing those transformations is difficult when little is known about the hidden components.

Existing approaches often impose properties such as statistical independence or probability-simplex structure on the components. The authors show that, under a carefully designed learning criterion, a nontrivial null space in the underlying mixing system suffices to identify and remove the unknown nonlinearity. This shifts the sufficient condition toward a property of the mixing system and substantially relaxes earlier identifiability requirements.

The paper also analyzes finite-sample behavior and proposes a block coordinate descent algorithm to implement its criterion. Numerical experiments support the theoretical claims. The result may help applications where strong structural knowledge about latent components is unavailable, while retaining the stated null-space condition. Its guarantee concerns identifying and removing the nonlinear transformation, a key step in understanding the underlying mixture.
neurips-2022-provable-subspace-identific.tldr: A nontrivial null space suffices under the proposed criterion to identify and remove post-mixture nonlinearities, relaxing assumptions on latent components.

paragraphs: Graph neural networks use relationships between nodes to improve predictions, yet graph information does not always help. Heterophily, where linked nodes have different labels, is often blamed. This paper argues that common homophily measures overlook something important by considering only agreement between graph connections and labels.

The authors instead examine node similarity after neighborhood aggregation and define new metrics from that perspective. They prove that local diversification can address some harmful forms of heterophily. Building on this analysis, their Adaptive Channel Mixing framework combines aggregation, diversification, and identity channels within each baseline GNN layer, adapting how these information sources are used.

Across ten node-classification benchmarks, adding ACM consistently yields significant performance gains. The augmented models exceed state-of-the-art GNNs on most tasks without substantial computational burden. The findings support examining what neighborhood processing does to node representations, rather than judging a graph solely by label agreement. They also show the value of giving each layer several ways to use local information.
neurips-2022-revisiting-heterophily-for-.tldr: Adaptive Channel Mixing combines aggregation, diversification, and identity information to improve node classification, guided by a revised analysis of heterophily.

paragraphs: Neural stochastic differential equations model representations that evolve with randomness. The paper identifies a difficulty when those representations take values on a manifold, a space with geometric structure that need not behave like ordinary Euclidean space. In that setting, conventional neural SDEs typically lose expressive power.

The proposed Riemannian neural SDE extends the conventional Euclidean formulation to express stochastic representations on manifolds. The central design choice is to make the geometry of the representation space part of the modeling framework. This directly addresses the mismatch identified by the authors between a manifold-valued representation and the usual Euclidean model.

Empirical evaluations across various tasks show significant improvements over the baseline methods. These results support the proposed extension as a way to model stochastic representations more effectively when their geometry matters. The contribution concerns the combination of randomness and manifold structure: the model retains the neural SDE approach while extending the space in which its representations are expressed. The reported performance gains provide empirical support for that geometric adaptation.
neurips-2022-riemannian-neural-sde-learn.tldr: Riemannian neural SDEs extend stochastic representation learning to manifolds and significantly outperform compared baselines in the reported tasks.

paragraphs: Recovering a three-dimensional scene usually benefits from viewing it from different positions. S³-NeRF instead uses multiple images taken from one viewpoint under different point lights. The changing illumination supplies evidence through shading and shadows, even though the camera position stays fixed.

The method learns a neural reflectance field representing both scene geometry and how surfaces reflect light. This goes beyond a depth or normal map describing only the visible surface. Its reconstruction process uses the two lighting cues to infer geometry, replacing the reliance on agreement between images captured from multiple viewpoints.

Experiments on challenging datasets show recovery of both visible and invisible portions of scene geometry. The representation is also reported to handle depth discontinuities robustly and support rendering from new viewpoints and under new lighting. These findings demonstrate the information available in changing illumination under the tested conditions. The input remains a set of differently lit images, so the single-view claim refers to a fixed viewpoint rather than a single photograph.
neurips-2022-s-3-nerf-neural-reflectance.tldr: S³-NeRF reconstructs geometry and reflectance from a fixed viewpoint under changing point lights by using shading and shadow cues.

paragraphs: Obtaining labels can be expensive, while some labels may already be available from a potentially biased collection process. This paper studies linear regression with both previously labeled examples and unlabeled examples whose labels can be actively requested. The aim is to approach the best full-data regression fit while making as few new queries as possible.

The authors introduce an instance-dependent quantity called reduced rank. Their efficient algorithm needs O(R_X/epsilon) label queries to achieve squared error within a factor of 1 + epsilon of the best linear fit. The query bound therefore reflects this property of the particular problem, while also making the cost of demanding greater accuracy explicit.

The result yields improved upper bounds for active ridge regression and active kernel ridge regression, where reduced rank corresponds to established dimension measures. For a distributional special case, the paper proves a matching instance-wise lower bound for every design matrix. In that setting, the dependence on reduced rank and accuracy captures both what the algorithm achieves and what any algorithm must pay.
neurips-2022-semi-supervised-active-line.tldr: Reduced rank characterizes label-query complexity for semi-supervised active linear regression, with a matching lower bound in a distributional special case.

paragraphs: Quantization reduces the numerical precision used by a neural network. For pretrained language models, many methods require end-to-end quantization-aware training with the full dataset, creating substantial time, memory, and data-access demands. This paper develops a post-training approach intended to reduce those costs.

Module-wise reconstruction error minimization divides the language model into multiple modules and minimizes the reconstruction error caused by quantization within each one. The authors also design a parallel training strategy that lets modules train locally on separate devices without waiting for preceding modules. This organization makes the adaptation process less dependent on sequential computation through the whole model.

On GLUE and SQuAD, the proposed method performs close to quantization-aware training while substantially reducing training time, memory overhead, and data consumption. Its parallel strategy achieves nearly the theoretical speedup, with roughly fourfold acceleration on four GPUs given as an example. The results support module-level reconstruction as a practical way to retain much of the predictive performance while making quantization substantially cheaper.
neurips-2022-towards-efficient-post-trai.tldr: Module-wise post-training quantization approaches quantization-aware training performance while reducing time, memory, and data needs in language-model evaluations.

paragraphs: Named entity recognition and disambiguation help systems identify mentions of entities and determine which entities those mentions refer to. These capabilities support applications such as information retrieval, question answering, and event detection. TweetNERD provides a shared dataset for evaluating this work specifically on tweets.

The dataset contains more than 340,000 tweets spanning 2010 through 2021. The authors describe it as the largest and most temporally diverse open-source benchmark for these tasks on tweets. Its evaluation setup covers three distinct problems: finding entity mentions, linking entities when the correct mention spans are supplied, and performing recognition and linking together.

The paper reports results from existing publicly available methods on specified dataset splits, giving researchers reference evaluations for future comparisons. Separating the three tasks allows evaluation of mention recognition, disambiguation with known spans, and the complete process. Released under a Creative Commons Attribution license, TweetNERD contributes an accessible evaluation resource whose scale and temporal coverage broaden the available basis for studying entity-focused language processing on tweets.
neurips-2022-tweetnerd-end-to-end-entity.tldr: TweetNERD provides over 340,000 tweets and evaluation setups for entity recognition, entity linking, and end-to-end linking.

paragraphs: Return-conditioned supervised learning turns offline reinforcement learning into a prediction problem. It learns action distributions conditioned on the current state and the total return of the recorded trajectory. At deployment, it requests actions associated with a high return. This paper examines when that procedure actually produces an optimal policy.

The authors establish optimality under a set of assumptions, but show that these assumptions are stronger than those required by traditional dynamic-programming approaches. They construct specific decision processes and datasets that illustrate why the assumptions are needed and where return conditioning reaches its limits. The analysis therefore separates a promising learning recipe from the conditions that justify its use.

Experiments in simple point-mass environments and on D4RL datasets provide evidence that the identified limitations can also affect practical performance. The findings do not say that return-conditioned learning always fails; they show that its success depends on more demanding conditions than an appealing supervised formulation alone might suggest. This gives a theoretical and empirical account of when its policy-selection strategy can be trusted to deliver optimal behavior.
neurips-2022-when-does-return-conditione.tldr: Return-conditioned supervised learning can recover optimal policies, but requires stronger assumptions than dynamic programming and exhibits corresponding practical limitations.
